Package com.stzteam.features.robotlocalization.fusion

Class StdDevStrategies

java.lang.Object
com.stzteam.features.robotlocalization.fusion.StdDevStrategies
public final class StdDevStrategies extends Object
Strategies for computing the confidence of a vision measurement.

Each strategy is a BiFunction<Double, Integer, Matrix<N3,N1>> going from (distance in metres, tag count) to [sigmaX, sigmaY, sigmaTheta], ready for addVisionMeasurement. You hand them to a source with PoseSource.setStdDevsStrategy(BiFunction).

They compose: a base strategy is wrapped in a dynamic degradation and the result is bounded with clamped(java.util.function.BiFunction<java.lang.Double, java.lang.Integer, edu.wpi.first.math.Matrix<edu.wpi.first.math.numbers.N3, edu.wpi.first.math.numbers.N1>>, double, double, double, double): 


 source.setStdDevsStrategy(
     StdDevStrategies.clamped(
         StdDevStrategies.dynamicStateDegradation(
             StdDevStrategies.quadraticContinuous(0.05, 0.10),
             drivetrain::getChassisSpeeds,
             3.0, 2.0),
         0.02, 4.0,    // sigma XY between 2 cm and 4 m
         0.02, 10.0)); // sigma theta between 0.02 and 10 rad

Always bound the final result. Multiplicative strategies have no ceiling of their own, and a runaway value --- or an Infinity --- breaks the Kalman filter's matrix inversion from the inside, with no error to say what happened.

    • quadraticContinuous

      public static BiFunction<Double,Integer,edu.wpi.first.math.Matrix<edu.wpi.first.math.numbers.N3,edu.wpi.first.math.numbers.N1>> quadraticContinuous(double baseXY, double baseTheta)
      The continuous quadratic, which is the usual recommendation in FRC.

      The error grows with the square of the distance --- a tag twice as far away covers a quarter of the pixels, and PnP degrades just as fast --- and drops with the number of visible tags.

      Parameters:
      baseXY - coefficient for X and Y.
      baseTheta - coefficient for the heading.
      Returns:
      the base * distance^2 / tags strategy.

    • interpolatedEmpirical

      public static BiFunction<Double,Integer,edu.wpi.first.math.Matrix<edu.wpi.first.math.numbers.N3,edu.wpi.first.math.numbers.N1>> interpolatedEmpirical(edu.wpi.first.math.interpolation.InterpolatingDoubleTreeMap xyMap, edu.wpi.first.math.interpolation.InterpolatingDoubleTreeMap thetaMap, List<StdDevStrategies.TagStep> tagSteps)
      Interpolates the base error from a curve measured in practice, then applies the tag-count multiplier.

      This is the best option if you went to the trouble of measuring: put the robot at known distances, note the real spread, and feed those points into the maps. WPILib interpolates between them and saturates at the last known point.

      Parameters:
      xyMap - map from distance (m) to sigma for X and Y (m).
      thetaMap - map from distance (m) to heading sigma (rad).
      tagSteps - tag-count bands.
      Returns:
      the empirical strategy.

    • dynamicStateDegradation

      public static BiFunction<Double,Integer,edu.wpi.first.math.Matrix<edu.wpi.first.math.numbers.N3,edu.wpi.first.math.numbers.N1>> dynamicStateDegradation(BiFunction<Double,Integer,edu.wpi.first.math.Matrix<edu.wpi.first.math.numbers.N3,edu.wpi.first.math.numbers.N1>> baseStrategy, Supplier<edu.wpi.first.math.kinematics.ChassisSpeeds> speedsSupplier, double maxSafeLinearMps, double maxSafeOmegaRads, double angularBias)
      Inflates the base error when the robot is moving, to account for blur and rolling-shutter distortion.

      Linear velocity penalises confidence in X and Y. Angular velocity penalises both, and harder: spinning fast, the tags come out skewed and PnP loses the rotation first, which is precisely the axis you can least afford to get wrong.

      The multipliers are internally bounded to 400 as a safety net, so this strategy cannot return Infinity even if the speed runs away. To really control the final range, wrap it in clamped(java.util.function.BiFunction<java.lang.Double, java.lang.Integer, edu.wpi.first.math.Matrix<edu.wpi.first.math.numbers.N3, edu.wpi.first.math.numbers.N1>>, double, double, double, double).

      Parameters:
      baseStrategy - strategy to inflate.
      speedsSupplier - the chassis' current speeds.
      maxSafeLinearMps - linear velocity above which the image degrades.
      maxSafeOmegaRads - angular velocity above which the tags come out skewed.
      angularBias - how much the angular excess weighs against the linear one. 2.0 is a reasonable starting point: spinning ruins the image more than driving.
      Returns:
      the inflated strategy.

      Creates a drift strategy for a VIO, on the FPGA clock.
      Parameters:
      baseXY - sigma for X and Y when freshly corrected.
      baseTheta - heading sigma when freshly corrected.
      driftPerSecondXY - metres of uncertainty added each second.

      the strategy, which must be reset after each correction.
